title: Invariant integral open schematic closure and its canonical function field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $X$ an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], and $f:X\to S$ a structure morphism. Let $P$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $r:P\to X$ be a morphism [def-pc-scheme]. Let a finite group $H$ act by scheme automorphisms $a_h$ on $X$, $A_h$ on $P$ and $b_h$ on $S$, all left actions, with $fa_h=b_hf$ and $rA_h=a_hr$; the $b_h$ arise from a field action using inverse field automorphisms under $\operatorname{Spec}$. Suppose $U\subset X$ is a dense invariant open and $r^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow P$ be the open immersion given by its inverse [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $c:T=\operatorname{SIm}(j)\hookrightarrow P$ be the scheme-theoretic image [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $T$ is the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline{j(|U|)}$, is nonempty and irreducible, and is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The factorization $j_T:U\to T$ of $j$ is a dense open immersion, and for $q=rc$ the restriction $q^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism of schemes. The defining ideal of $T$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] is preserved by every $A_h$. There is a unique left action $a^T_h:T\to T$ by scheme automorphisms with $ca^T_h=A_hc$; it satisfies $qa^T_h=a_hq$ and $fqa^T_h=b_hfq$. If $\eta_T$ and $\eta_X$ are the generic points [def-sc-generic-point], then $q(\eta_T)=\eta_X$ and the actual stalk map $q^\sharp_{\eta_T}:\mathcal O_{X,\eta_X}\to\mathcal O_{T,\eta_T}$ is an isomorphism of fields, hence gives the canonical identification $k(X)\simeq k(T)$ [def-sc-function-field]. No normality, geometric integrality, projectivity or faithfulness of an action is assumed.

source.place: Tag 056B, lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-reduced; Tag 01R8, lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image, including restriction to an open and the ideal kernel; Tag 01RW, definition-function-field, and Tag 01RV, lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions. Returned proof steps 6 (closure and restriction), 7 (invariant ideal and descended action), and 9 (generic stalk map); action descent is agent-explicit.

proof.text: Write $i:U\hookrightarrow X$ and $W=r^{-1}(U)\subseteq P$. The given inverse identifies $U$ with the open subscheme $W$, so $j$ is an open immersion with image $W$. Since $X$ is nonempty and $U$ is dense, $U$ is nonempty. Its stalks are the corresponding reduced stalks of $X$, and any two nonempty opens of $U$ are nonempty opens of the irreducible space $X$ and hence intersect. Thus $U$ is integral. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], every open subscheme of the Noetherian scheme $P$ is quasi-compact. In particular for every affine open $V\subseteq P$, $j^{-1}(V)$ is isomorphic to the open subscheme $W\cap V$ of $P$ and is quasi-compact. This proves that $j$ is quasi-compact.

By [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image], the ideal defining the specified $T=\operatorname{SIm}(j)$ is the largest quasi-coherent ideal contained in $\ker(\mathcal O_P\to j_*\mathcal O_U)$; since $j$ is quasi-compact, it is this sheaf kernel itself. Thus the image and canonical factor in the following citations are the specified $T,c,j_T$. Apply [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image] to the reduced source $U$: $T$ is the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline{j(|U|)}$. This space is nonempty and irreducible: if two opens meet the closure, each meets $j(U)$, and their intersections with $j(U)$ meet since $U$ is irreducible. Therefore $T$ is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The quasi-compact open immersion $j$ is in particular an immersion; [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image] gives that its canonical factor $j_T:U\to T$ is an open immersion with dense image, and $cj_T=j$.

The equality $qj_T=i$ follows from $q=rc$ and $rj=i$. For $t\in T$, $q(t)\in U$ if and only if $c(t)\in W=j(U)$. Since a closed immersion is injective on underlying points and $cj_T=j$, this is equivalent to $t\in j_T(U)$. Consequently the open subscheme $q^{-1}(U)$ is exactly the open image of $j_T$. By the definition of open immersion, $j_T:U\to q^{-1}(U)$ is an isomorphism. The equation $qj_T=i$ says that its inverse is the specified restriction $q^{-1}(U)\to U$.

source.place: Tag 01R8 (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image), restriction to the open W; here the common-open assertion is proved directly from the open factor and injectivity of c.

proof.text: Fix $h\in H$ and write $u_h=a_h|_U$. Equivariance of $r$ and invariance of $U$ imply $A_h(W)=W$ and $A_hj=ju_h$: on $W$, both maps are determined by their composite with the isomorphism $r|_W:W\to U$. The morphism $c_h=A_{h^{-1}}c:T\to P$ is a closed immersion, since composing a closed immersion with an isomorphism preserves its defining closed embedding and surjective structure-sheaf map. It gives the closed factorization $c_h(j_Tu_h)=A_{h^{-1}}ju_h=j$. Apply [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-universal] to this factorization of $j$: there is a unique $v_h:T\to T$ with $c_hv_h=c$, hence $cv_h=A_hc$.

source.place: Tag 01R6 (lemma-scheme-theoretic-image), minimal closed factor; agent-explicit translated closed factorization, as in lemma-factor-factor.

proof.text: A closed immersion is a monomorphism: its injective point map determines any factoring point map, and locally the surjection onto its structure sheaf determines any factoring sheaf map. Cancel $c$ in $cv_e=c$, $cv_hv_g=A_hA_gc=A_{hg}c$ and $cv_hv_{h^{-1}}=c$. Thus $v_e=1$, $v_hv_g=v_{hg}$ and $v_{h^{-1}}=v_h^{-1}$. Also $cv_hj_T=A_hj=ju_h=cj_Tu_h$, so cancellation gives $v_hj_T=j_Tu_h$: the descended action restricts to the prescribed action on the common open. Set $a_h^T=v_h$; these are the unique automorphisms with the required compatibility. Composition with $r$ and $f$ gives $qa_h^T=a_hq$ and $fqa_h^T=b_hfq$. For the defining ideal $\mathcal I(V)=\ker(c^\sharp_V)$ of [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], the square $ca_h^T=A_hc$ gives $c^\sharp_{A_h^{-1}V}A_h^\sharp_V=(a_h^T)^\sharp_{c^{-1}V}c^\sharp_V$. Both horizontal pullbacks are isomorphisms, so $A_h^\sharp_V$ carries $\mathcal I(V)$ onto $\mathcal I(A_h^{-1}V)$ for every open $V\subseteq P$. This is preservation of the defining ideal, as a sheaf, by $A_h$.

source.place: Tag 01HK (definition-closed-immersion-locally-ringed-spaces), kernel and surjection; elementary cancellation and kernel calculation for the constructed maps.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-scheme-sober], the integral schemes $U,X,T$ have unique generic points. Let $\eta_U$ be that of $U$. The closure in $X$ of $i(\eta_U)$ contains $i(U)$, because its intersection with the open subspace $i(U)$ is closed and contains a point dense there. Since $U$ is dense in $X$, this closure is $X$, so $i(\eta_U)=\eta_X$. The identical argument for the dense open $j_T$ gives $j_T(\eta_U)=\eta_T$. Evaluating $qj_T=i$ at $\eta_U$ proves $q(\eta_T)=\eta_X$.

source.place: Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober); elementary closure-of-a-singleton argument for the two dense open embeddings.

proof.text: For an open immersion, the stalk map is the identity under restriction to the open image: neighbourhoods contained in that image are cofinal among all neighbourhoods of the point, with the same rings of sections and restriction maps. Thus $i^\sharp_{\eta_U}$ and $(j_T)^\sharp_{\eta_U}$ are isomorphisms. Taking germs in $qj_T=i$ gives $(j_T)^\sharp_{\eta_U}\circ q^\sharp_{\eta_T}=i^\sharp_{\eta_U}$; hence the actual stalk map is $q^\sharp_{\eta_T}=((j_T)^\sharp_{\eta_U})^{-1}\circ i^\sharp_{\eta_U}$ and is an isomorphism. By [lem-sc-rational-functions-generic-stalks] these generic stalks of the integral schemes $X,T$ are fields, and by [def-sc-function-field] they are $k(X),k(T)$. This proves precisely the canonical function-field identification induced by $q$.

source.place: Tag 01RV (lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions), Tag 01RW (definition-function-field); elementary cofinal-neighbourhood stalk comparison and functoriality of germs.
